Adieu, Google Maps: Magic Earth Gets Major Update With Traffic, Road Sign Improvements
14 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Magic Lane
I’ve said it before, and I’m going to say it again: if you’re looking for a Google Maps replacement and don’t check out Magic Earth, you’re probably skipping the best alternative. And the most recent update is just a reminder.
The application was bumped to version 9.5.7, and the update includes improvements for several key features, including how it shows traffic on the map, road signs, and weather information.
If you’re already a Magic Earth user, the first change you’ll notice after you install the update is additional traffic data you see on the screen.
The application now shows the delay for your active route right next to the remaining time in the journey info panel. You can tap this new info to see additional details, such as the next traffic jam, the distance until you’re supposed to encounter it, and the delay it adds to your ETA.
Next, you’ll also see more upcoming road signs appearing on the map. I’ve always said that this feature - no matter if it’s in Magic Earth, Waze, Google Maps, or Apple Maps - is one of the essential tools a driver should get in a navigation app. We get more time to slow down and approach an intersection more carefully, so the likelihood of a crash, even if someone else breaks the law, is much lower.
Photo: Magic Lane Magic Earth will now show not only traffic lights, but also give way signs, stops, and even crosswalks.
The application has also tweaked how it shows roadblocks. If you expand the info panel for a route, you should see all the roadblocks you’re supposed to come across when you drive. The navigation panel at the top of the screen also highlights an upcoming roadblock, along with the distance to its location. Eventually, Magic Earth offers to take a detour or keep the current route.
This update also includes smaller refinements and one big feature for Premium users. If you have a subscription, you can now see the weather on arrival, with the forecast displayed for either your next stop or the final destination. If you tap this weather info icon, you can see additional details, such as the feels-like value, wind, and humidity.
Furthermore, Magic Earth has also received a feature that others have been offering for quite some time: the option to see the ETA to the next stop instead of the final destination. You can enable this feature to see the time, distance, and ETA to the next stop, so if you have a multi-stop route, you’ll know precisely how far you are from your next stop.
The new version is available on the App Store , and if you previously enabled automatic app updates on your device, you might already be running it.
